# Fun Science Experiments for 5 Year Olds (Glitter + Slime Approved!)
All use mostly household items, with optional low-cost buys if you don't have supplies on hand. All steps <10, safe for little hands with adult supervision.

---
## 1. Glitter Volcano (For the glitter lover!)
### What you need:
✅ Household stuff: Empty small plastic soda/water bottle, baking soda, white vinegar, red/orange food coloring, old tray/baking sheet, spoon
🛒 Optional buys (if you don't have them): Extra fine glitter ($1 at dollar store)
### How to do it:
1. Set your empty bottle on the tray to catch messy eruptions
2. Pour 2 tablespoons of baking soda into the bottom of the bottle
3. Add 3 drops of red food coloring and a big handful of glitter to the bottle
4. Pour ¼ cup of vinegar into the bottle, step back, and watch your sparkly volcano blow!
5. (Bonus) Add more vinegar + baking soda to make it erupt over and over
### Fun kid fact: The fizz is carbon dioxide gas, the same stuff that makes soda bubbly!

---
## 2. Glitter Lava Lamp (For the glitter lover!)
### What you need:
✅ Household stuff: Clear glass jar, water, vegetable oil, food coloring, spoon
🛒 Optional buys (if you don't have them): Alka-Seltzer tablets ($2 for 12-pack at grocery store), extra glitter ($1)
### How to do it:
1. Fill the jar ⅓ full of water
2. Pour vegetable oil on top until the jar is almost full, wait 1 minute for oil and water to separate
3. Add 2 drops of your favorite food coloring, watch it sink through the oil to the water
4. Dump a big spoonful of glitter into the jar
5. Break one Alka-Seltzer tablet into 4 small pieces, drop one piece in and watch glitter bubbles float up like lava!
6. When bubbles stop, drop another piece in for more magic
### Fun kid fact: Oil and water don't mix because oil is lighter than water!

---
## 3. Fluffy Glitter Slime (Perfect for both glitter + slime fans!)
### What you need:
✅ Household stuff: White school glue, baking soda, bowl, spoon, food coloring
🛒 Optional buys (if you don't have them): Travel-sized contact lens solution (with boric acid, $3), extra glitter ($1)
### How to do it:
1. Pour ½ cup of white glue into your bowl
2. Add 3 drops of food coloring and as much glitter as you want, stir well
3. Mix in ¼ teaspoon of baking soda until fully combined
4. Add 1 tablespoon of contact lens solution, stir fast until slime pulls away from the bowl
5. Knead the slime with your hands for 1 minute (if sticky, add 1 more drop of contact solution)
6. Stretch it, squish it, bounce it – it's yours!
### Fun kid fact: Slime is a non-Newtonian fluid, which means it acts like both a liquid and a solid!

---
## 4. Slime Bubble Blowing Contest (For the slime lover!)
### What you need:
✅ Household stuff: The slime you just made (or store-bought slime), drinking straws
🛒 Optional buys (if you don't have them): Extra glitter ($1 to sprinkle for sparkle)
### How to do it:
1. Flatten your slime into a ½-inch thick pancake on the table
2. Stick one end of the straw into the center of the slime pancake, pinch slime around the straw to seal it
3. Blow gently into the other end of the straw, watch your slime bubble get bigger and bigger!
4. (Contest idea) See who can blow the biggest bubble without it popping!
5. Sprinkle glitter on your bubbles to make them sparkly before they pop
### Fun kid fact: The stretchy slime traps the air you blow in, making the bubble grow!

---
## Total max cost if you need all optional supplies: ~$7 (all available at dollar stores or local grocery stores)
Note: None of these use harsh chemicals, just make sure the kids don't eat any of the supplies!
